tests.description: A rejected approval starts no job, and the rejection keeps its rejected flag. This fails if startJob starts the job before raising the plan's questions.
startJob's question says the command runs in the background. safeBash's question for the same command does not.
startJob returns the job id at once. jobOutput with wait returns when the job ends, with its exit code and all its output. A second read returns no output, because it was already returned.
stopJob stops a running job and returns its final report. The report counts as read, so the job is no longer unread.
A time guard that runs out during a jobOutput wait raises std::guard, so the handler is asked. Rejecting it makes the guarded block a failure, and the job keeps running.
Approving the guard trip with more time lets the block finish with the report the wait returned when it was cut short. This fails if the wait throws on a guard trip.
A handler that rejects a guard trip during a jobOutput wait leaves the job's output unread, so the next read returns it.
A command that does not run under bash, such as echo, runs in the foreground with a line saying so. No job is started, and no question says background.
jobOutput and stopJob for an id the run does not know return a failure that says there is no such job and lists the jobs that exist. Neither throws.
A working directory that does not exist gives the failure safeBash gives, and no job is started.
The question for a job carries the job's limit in milliseconds as its timeout.
